newsitem.title: POLAND: NBP weakens bullish zloty, one-day depos fall.
newsitem.headline: NBP weakens bullish zloty, one-day depos fall.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland intervened against the zloty for the third day running on Monday to stop its rise fuelled by large-scale foreign investor entry at the primary T-bill tender, dealers said.

Delears estimated foreign bids at the 1.3 billion zloty auction at $350 million, a part of which found its way onto the interbank forex market, propelling the zloty past NBP-accepted levels of around 2.5 pecent from the trading band centre.
"The zloty charged on foreign bids at the primary tender, but once the NBP bought all that foreigners wanted to sell, the market calmed down," said Tomasz Nowakowski of Bank Handlowy.
Dealers estimated the central bank bought some $40 million on the market, bringing the zloty down to 2.46/2.43 percent from the parity rate from around 2.52 percent when it first stepped in.
The zloty closed at 3.1300/14 to the dollar, up from 3.1385/05 on Friday and at 1.8365/71 to the mark, down from 1.8275/80.

Dealers said the market might see more NBP action tomorrow as some foreigners, who bought an estimated $250 million at the primary T-bill tender after bidding for more than $350 million, may exchange currencies into zlotys to pay for the bills.

"Tomorrow may again be nervous because some of those who bought the bills today may be exchanging currencies to pay for them with a tomorrow/next value date," said Piotr Czyzewski, forex dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
Demand at the T-bill tender totalled 4.7 billion zlotys against a 1.3 billion offer and all minimum prices rose for the first time in months.
"Good March inflation data and even better forecasts as well as the relative weakeness of the zloty make zloty instruments very attractive to foreigners," a T-bill dealer at a major bank here said.
Year-on-year inflation fell to 16.6 percent in March from 17.3 percent in February and is widely expected to drop to 13 percent in December.

On the money market O/N fell to 20.50/20.70 percent from 21.25 percent at opening while T/N eased to 20.70/21.00 percent from 21.40/21.60 percent despite a 699 million zloty net outflow after the NBP refrained all drainages.

"The high liquidity is puzzling, especially that tomorrow is the bulk of banks' monthly tax payments. But I expect rates may ease even further tomorrow," said Aleksandra Watroba of Bank Slaski SA. -- Jan Strupczewski +48 22 653 9700
